source: Every uncommon word on the pages, in one sentence. Hebrew terms follow common Ashkenazi and Israeli usage in English-speaking communities.
words: Community. A congregation, or the people who count as yours.
Giving to those in need. From the word for justice, not charity: something owed, not something extra.
A tenth. The ordinary share of income given as tzedakah.
A fifth. The generous share, and the most the tradition asks.
An interest-free loan fund. Short for gemilut chasadim, acts of loving-kindness.
An accounting of the soul: taking stock of the year, usually in Elul.
The last month of the Jewish year, the month before Rosh Hashanah, for taking stock.
The new moon, the first of each Hebrew month. A small monthly marker.
Food gifts to friends on Purim.
Gifts to people in need on Purim, one of the day's four mitzvot.
Wheat money: giving so others can afford Pesach.
The anniversary of a death, marked with a candle and often a gift.
The burial society that prepares a body for a Jewish funeral.
A small, usually lay-led community that prays and eats together.
A price that depends on what you can pay. Asking for it is expected, not embarrassing.
The people who are your family because you chose each other, whatever the law says.
A court order that makes a non-biological parent a legal parent, honored in every state.
A paper naming who decides your medical care if you cannot.
A paper naming who handles your money if you cannot, while you are alive.
The person named on an account or policy to receive it at your death. Beats the will.
A health savings account: untaxed savings for medical costs, for people on a high-deductible plan. Rolls over.
A flexible spending account through work: untaxed money for medical costs, mostly use-it-or-lose-it within the year.
The most a health plan makes you pay in a year for covered care. After it, the plan pays all.
The yearly rate a loan or card charges, as a percent.
Someone who promises to repay a loan if you cannot. What a gemach asks for instead of a credit score.
Insemination in a clinic, timed to a cycle. The simpler, cheaper fertility procedure.
Eggs fertilized outside the body and transferred. The bigger, costlier procedure.
One partner's eggs, the other partner carries.
A blank box means 'not entered yet'. A typed 0 means 'zero'. The pages never treat a blank as a number.
